extracted.intended_audience: readers/students of classical literature and Cervantes' Don Quixote
extracted.subtask_description: A chunk of Cervantes' Don Quixote (late chapters) containing comic episodes, authorial commentary on books/poets/painters, and character dialogue that expresses implicit criteria about writing, relevance, and style. Useful for extracting norms about literary quality and comic technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book longevity depends on quality (good, faithful, true)
rubrics_metrics.description: "If it should be good, faithful, and true, it will have ages of life; but if it should be bad, from its birth to its burial will not be a very long journey."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The passage presents a criterion for judging histories/books: fidelity and truthfulness (and general goodness) determine whether a work will endure. Implies that accuracy and faithfulness to subject matter are measures of a work's lasting worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic relevance and originality (avoid pilfering)
rubrics_metrics.description: "With the callow poets of our day the way is for every one to write as he pleases and pilfer where he chooses, whether it be germane to the matter or not, and now-a-days there is no piece of silliness they can sing or write that is not set down to poetic licence."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit critique: poets should not randomly appropriate material or insert irrelevant/silly passages under the excuse of 'poetic licence.' Relevance to the subject and originality are implied standards; irrelevant borrowing is an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose quotations and stanzas appropriate to subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Don Quixote: "what you sang did not seem to me very much to the purpose; for what have Garcilasso’s stanzas to do with the death of this lady?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted material (poems, stanzas, songs) should bear on the episode or theme being treated. Mismatched or ill-timed quotations undermine coherence and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial care and responsibility (avoid laissez-faire production)
rubrics_metrics.description: About a careless painter/writer: "Whatever it might turn out; and if he chanced to paint a cock he would write under it, 'This is a cock,' for fear they might think it was a fox."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creators should not be indifferent about their work's outcome or rely on labels to mask poor execution. Take responsibility for clarity and intentionality in production rather than leaving things to chance or crude signage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid haphazard responses / superficial erudition
rubrics_metrics.description: Of a poet called Mauleon: "who used to answer at haphazard whatever he was asked, and on one asking him what Deum de Deo meant, he replied Dé donde diere."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responding carelessly or feigning erudition is an anti-pattern. Accuracy and thoughtfulness are expected when explaining, translating, or commenting — sloppy or glib answers reflect poorly on a writer/speaker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer plain, simple, straightforward speech over excessive proverbialism
rubrics_metrics.description: Don Quixote admonishes Sancho: "speak in a plain, simple, straight-forward way, as I have often told thee, and thou wilt find the good of it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overuse of proverbs or continual reliance on set phrases can obscure meaning; plainness and directness are recommended for clarity and effective communication, especially in didactic or persuasive contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivative continuations/pastiche judged harshly when low-quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Altisidora's vision: devils identify a book as "the 'Second Part of the History of Don Quixote of La Mancha,' not by Cide Hamete... 'So bad is it... that if I had set myself deliberately to make a worse, I could not have done it.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A poor sequel, imitation, or unauthorized continuation of a beloved work will be judged severely; derivative works should respect the original's standards of quality, or they risk being ridiculed as worthless.
